title: Venus over the BlackGEM telescopes
caption: Venus over the BlackGEM telescopes, La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Venus shines brightly over ESO's La Silla Observatory in this photo taken just before dawn, looking east. The sky also shows the soft zodiacal light, which is sunlight bounced off tiny grains of dust spread through the Solar System. To the left of the road stand the three domes of the BlackGEM telescopes.

Radboud University, KU Leuven and the Netherlands Research School for Astronomy (NOVA) built BlackGEM. Its task is to hunt for the fading glow left by some of the Universe's most violent events, such as collisions of black holes and neutron stars.

Such crashes send ripples through space and time that the LIGO and Virgo observatories can detect. Thanks to their wide field of view, the BlackGEM telescopes can spot the visible glow left behind by these events and so pinpoint where each collision took place.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: The camera exposure gathers more light than the eye, so the faint zodiacal light shows more clearly here than it would to someone standing on the mountain before dawn.

explore: Knowing where a merger happened lets astronomers study in greater detail what goes on when black holes and neutron stars merge, adding visible light to the ripples in spacetime that first announced the event.
alt: A bright planet shines in a pre-dawn sky with diffuse zodiacal light, above a road with three telescope domes on its left.
